messages:
elaine: heads up — hitting a weird behavior in the Go SDK generator sample app. when the HTTP request is canceled the generator stream still emits a few chunks afterwards and the client goroutine never returns. seems like a ctx leak. repro attached :facepalm:

elaine: minimal repro (simplified):
```go
func Serve(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    ctx := r.Context() // request ctx
    iter := client.Generator("gpt-small").Stream(ctx, Prompt{Text: "story"})
    // spawn a goroutine to consume so we can flush to client
    go func() {
        for iter.Next() {
            token := iter.Text()
            _, _ = w.Write([]byte(token))
        }
        if err := iter.Err(); err != nil {
            log.Println("iter error:", err)
        }
    }()
}
```

elaine: if I cancel the request (client closes tab) the response writer panics with "write tcp: use of closed network connection" and then a few seconds later the generator still produces tokens and never stops.

ryan: can you paste the SDK logs around the cancel? :eyes:

elaine: logs:
```
2026-03-22T15:02:10Z INFO dialed model backend 
2026-03-22T15:02:11Z INFO auth refresh started (background)
2026-03-22T15:02:11Z DEBUG recv chunk: "Once upon a"
2026-03-22T15:02:12Z ERROR write failed: write tcp 10.0.0.1:443->10.0.0.2:55000: use of closed network connection
2026-03-22T15:02:15Z DEBUG recv chunk: " time, there was"
2026-03-22T15:02:16Z DEBUG recv chunk: " a small bot"
2026-03-22T15:02:20Z INFO stream closed by server
```

priya: is this the streaming iterator (Next()/Text()) or some pull-based API?

elaine: streaming iterator. code uses iter.Next() as above. i think the auth refresh kicks off on a background goroutine and it uses context.Background() so it keeps the connection alive even after request ctx cancel.

samir: hmm — two things could be happening: 1) the goroutine consuming tokens doesn't check the req ctx after a write failure and keeps calling Next() which reads from the transport buffer; 2) auth refresh / reconnect path runs with a non-cancellable ctx which re-establishes the stream. both would explain continued tokens.

samir: quick diagnosis: add a select around writes to bail when ctx.Done() fires, and make auth refresh take a parent ctx param. e.g. patch:
```diff
- go refreshAuth() // background, uses background ctx
+ go refreshAuth(ctx) // accept request ctx so refresh cancels with request
```

samir: and in consumer: 
```go
for {
    select {
    case <-ctx.Done():
        return
    default:
    }
    if !iter.Next() { break }
    // attempt write, but also respect ctx when write blocked
}
```

elaine: tried a quick local change: passing the request ctx into the auth refresh path stopped the reconnect and the iterator shutdown immediately after next returned false. looks promising. i'll open a proper PR with tests.

priya: nice. could be an onboarding doc update too — our sample app uses Background in a few places which teaches bad habits. recommend we audit sampleapps/ for Context.Background() usage in network auth paths.

ci-bot: CI: test/go-sdk-streaming: build passed in 32s :white_check_mark:

elaine: opened issue and draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4321 — includes repro, unit test that simulates client disconnect, and a patch to propagate ctx into token refresh + a small consumer change.

ryan: thanks for the clear repro. can we also add a quick note in the Go SDK README about iterator semantics and cancellation patterns? i had a couple internal chats where people assumed cancel auto-stops everything.

elaine: yeah adding a tiny section: "Respect request contexts in long-lived callbacks/auth" + a snippet showing the select. i'll add to PR.

samir: also add an integration test for auth-refresh race where token expiry triggers mid-stream. that caught similar issues before.

elaine: will do. thanks all. :raised_hands:
